<description>
Follow-up to #35675. This addresses the `getblocktemplate` part of the "Remove remaining global states" TODO in #33758, as suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35675#pullrequestreview-5299625960.

`getblocktemplate` reuses its last template until the tip changes, or until the mempool changes and the template is more than 5 seconds old. That cache currently lives in four function-local statics, which:

- live as long as the process, so the cached `CBlockIndex*` can outlive its `ChainstateManager` (as in unit tests);
- rely on `cs_main` being held, which nothing checks;
- can't be unit tested.

This PR moves the cache into `BlockTemplateManager`, in three commits:

1. **rpc:** refactors the statics in place into a `CachedBlockTemplate` struct and a `GetNewOrCachedBlockTemplate()` helper, `GUARDED_BY(::cs_main)`. The template's `hashPrevBlock` replaces the cached `CBlockIndex*`, and the 5 seconds becomes `GBT_TEMPLATE_REBUILD_INTERVAL`.
2. **refactor:** moves them into `BlockTemplateManager`. It's easiest to review with `git show --color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change`.
3. **test:** adds a unit test for each rebuild rule and for the retry after a failed build.

No behavior change is intended, and only `getblocktemplate` uses the cache. It uses `cs_main` rather than its own mutex, since the RPC already holds it and building a template takes it anyway.
</description>

[2026-11-13] rc:4561855353 inline on src/node/block_template_manager.h by enirox001 (contributor) (edited 2026-11-13):
In commit https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36356/changes/56078a5bf728cd48882a17b49e6079267178698b: _refactor: move getblocktemplate cache into BlockTemplateManager_

I think would be useful to cover is the change in cache lifetime. The existing test checks when a manager reuses or rebuilds its template, but everything happens within the same manager instance.

Previously, the cache was process wide, so destroying and recreating the manager wouldn’t clear that state. Now that the cache belongs to `BlockTemplateManager`, a new instance should start with an empty cache, even if the chain tip and mempool haven’t changed. That seems like one of the main benefits of this refactor, so it would be good to protect it with a test.

I’ve included a small possible patch to achieve this:
```diff --git a/src/test/miner_tests.cpp b/src/test/miner_tests.cpp
index 5afa32f8a0..2a455bf53c 100644
--- a/src/test/miner_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/miner_tests.cpp
@@ -1048,4 +1048,26 @@ BOOST_FIXTURE_TEST_CASE(block_template_manager_cached_template, RegTestingSetup)
     BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(fifth.block_template->block.hashPrevBlock, new_tip);
 }

+BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(block_template_manager_cache_lifetime)
+{
+    LOCK(::cs_main);
+
+    Assert(m_node.mempool)->AddTransactionsUpdated(1);
+    const auto first{Assert(m_node.block_template_manager)->GetNewOrCachedBlockTemplate()};
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(first.block_template);
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(first.transactions_updated != 0);
+
+    m_node.block_template_manager.reset();
+    CreateBlockTemplateManager();
+
+    auto& manager{*Assert(m_node.block_template_manager)};
+    BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(manager.GetCachedTransactionsUpdated(), 0);
+
+    const auto second{Assert(m_node.block_template_manager)->GetNewOrCachedBlockTemplate()};
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(second.block_template);
+    BOOST_CHECK(second.block_template != first.block_template);
+
+    BOOST_CHECK(manager.GetNewOrCachedBlockTemplate().block_template == second.block_template);
+}
+
 BOOST_AUTO_TEST_SUITE_END()
```

this would build a template, destroy the manager, and create a replacement. It would then check that the replacement’s cached mempool counter starts at zero and that its first request produces a different template object. The original template is kept alive through its shared pointer, so its address cannot be reusued and accidentally affect the comparison.

[2026-11-13] r:5888991286 review COMMENTED by enirox001 (contributor):
Code Review https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36356/changes/b7a6cf47363c01d7507601bdb09847f90aaf2c59

The cache fits better in `BlockTemplateManager` since this is already where templates are created. Its lifetime now follows the manager, instead of leaving cache state around in the rpc statics.

I think the shared template gives us room to shorten the `cs_main` critical section in a followup. At the moment, `getblocktemplate` holds the lock while encoding transactions, calculating their dependencies, and constructing the response. Most of that work only needs the template we already obtained.

With `shared_ptr<const CBlockTemplate>`, a request can keep reading its template after releasing the lock. Another request could rebuild the cache without destroying the template the first request is using. Previously, simply unlocking around that work would have been unsafe because replacing the static `unique_ptr` could invalidate what the first request was reading.

We’d still need to collect the chain dependent information before unlocking. But moving the transaction encoding and response construction outside that section seems worth exploring, especially with multiple clients calling `getblocktemplate`.
